name: The Shore Club Turks and Caicos
positioning: Beach resort on Long Bay Beach, the quieter side of Providenciales, with clear, shallow water, suites and residences, and a wellness focus
best_for: Families who want a kids' club and clear, shallow water
Travelers who want a quieter beach than Grace Bay

facts.text: The Shore Club is at 13 Sea Breeze Close on Long Bay Beach, Providenciales.
Long Bay Beach is the quieter counterpoint to Grace Bay, on the opposite side of Providenciales.
Accommodations range from Garden, Pool and Ocean View suites to one- to three-bedroom residences and a handful of penthouses.
The oceanfront one-bedroom suite has a generous kitchen, an airy living room, a spa-like bathroom with a tiled shower and a big soaking tub, and a king bed.
The pools are spaced out by lush tropical greenery, and beach loungers are spread far apart.
Sui-Ren is the hotel's signature restaurant, serving Japanese cuisine with Peruvian influences.
Breakfast is served at Almond Tree, an indoor-outdoor space that also serves dinner.
Accessible pathways cover many shared spaces, including restaurants, pools and beachfront areas, with elevator access in multi-level buildings.

highlights.text: The water at Long Bay is strikingly clear and remarkably shallow, so you can walk far out toward the buoys.
Guests get complimentary non-motorized water sports equipment such as snorkels, sea kayaks, paddle boards and Hobie Cats.
At the Dune Spa, massages and other treatments take place in little huts.
Beyond the Dune Spa there is a lap pool and gym beside the yoga pavilion, and tennis courts that can be reserved for tennis and pickleball.
The complimentary Jungle Jam kids' club offers half and full days of activities for ages 4 to 12.

considerations.text: The best bet for getting around is a taxi, and taxis are not cheap.
The Dune Spa's facilities are small.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
